_what: Adjudicated shape matches for the magnitude-guard sweep (PERF-02 / F37).
_read_this_first: is listed here with a written reason. tools/gate/check_magnitude_guard.py fails when a
SUSPECT match (non-zero threshold, no asserting else branch) appears that is not listed,
and also fails when a listed entry matches nothing any more -- so a fixed guard cannot
leave a stale allowance behind that silently re-accepts a different guard later.
Entries are keyed on file + whitespace-normalised condition + ordinal, NOT on line
numbers and NOT on raw bytes: line numbers move whenever anything above a guard is
edited, and core.autocrlf=true means the tracked bytes differ between checkouts.
The two guards F27 actually FIXED (d85ec1d) are deliberately absent -- see _f27_fixed.
Adding a new entry here is a review decision, not a formality. Write the reason.

_f27_fixed.note: 50-page baseline measures ~0.0145s, so the EXPECT_LT(big/small, 15.0) never ran. Guard deleted; replaced by a measured scaling-exponent bound. No longer a shape match.
100-page open measures ~12-16ms, so the ratio assertion never ran. Guard deleted; assertion unconditional. No longer a shape match.

_i273_fixed.note: The signal count was already asserted by EXPECT_EQ on the line above; the `if` existed only because EXPECT_ continues past a failure and takeFirst() would then run on an empty list. Promoted to ASSERT_EQ and the body made unconditional, so the emitted position is now always checked.
Same shape: the count was asserted with EXPECT_EQ, then re-tested in an `if` purely to keep .at(0) in range. Promoted to ASSERT_EQ; the argument-value check now always runs.

Gated on the edited text being unique on the page so a coincidental repeat could not misfire. The intent was right but as a runtime `if` it meant a drifting fixture silently disarmed the check. Uniqueness is a fact about a controlled fixture PDF, so it is now an ASSERT_EQ precondition and the real property is checked unconditionally.

Gated the location check on there being exactly one definition, so a helper with TWO definitions — the state the guard exists to catch — had neither copy examined. Replaced with a loop over every definition found, which checks all of them on every path. Deliberately not ASSERT_: it sits inside a loop over all helper names and a fatal assertion would stop reporting the rest.

Gated the last-page render on the document being multi-page, so every single-page file in the corpus asserted nothing. No condition is needed: for a one-page file pageCount-1 is 0, a valid index. Made unconditional, and the pageCount precondition promoted to ASSERT_GT so a zero-page document cannot reach createDisplayList(-1).

Gated the second setPage on the fixture being multi-page. The fixture is test_3page.pdf, so its page count is a fact to assert rather than a condition to hope for. ASSERT_GT on the count, then setPage(1) unconditionally.

This was a TAUTOLOGY: `if (quads.size() > 1) EXPECT_GT(quads.size(), 1)` restated its own guard and could never fail, while the whole body being gated meant a selection capturing zero or one quad asserted nothing in a test named MultiLineSelection. The 250pt span is deliberate, so the multi-line property is now asserted unconditionally.

SECURITY-RELEVANT. Gated the account-name leak assertion on the name being determinable and >= 3 characters, so on a host where GetUserNameW fails or the name is very short, the check that a committed artifact carries no account name passed WITHOUT LOOKING. Both cases are unusable input, not a satisfied property, so they now FAIL via ASSERT_. The name is also no longer interpolated into the failure message — offset and length only — because a leak check that prints what it hunts becomes the next producer in CI logs.
Second instance of the same defect in the same file, same remedy. See the ordinal-0 entry above.

Zero-threshold presence guard, not a measurement magnitude: it asks whether the allowlist holds any real (non-underscore) entry before requiring each one to carry a 'max' cap. With zero concessions there is nothing to cap, so the requirement is vacuously satisfied rather than skipped, and the allowlist is deliberately empty (GitHub #199/#272) — a state the surrounding case asserts separately. Cannot become permanently false as hardware gets faster. Proven to discriminate: an uncapped real entry reddens the case, a capped one does not, an empty allowlist passes.

_ownership.why_permanent: These 31 are ADJUDICATED shape matches, not defects: each was read and found to be a legitimate numeric-literal comparison guarding an assertion, which is why the file calls them 'adjudicated' rather than 'known-bad'. There is nothing to burn down -- driving this to 0 would mean deleting correct tests. This differs from reachability_skip_baseline.json, where each entry IS a test not asserting, and from GitHub #118, where each entry IS a leak on an error path.
_ownership.what_would_change_this: A new entry is NOT automatically acceptable. The guard fails on growth so every addition is a deliberate edit; the reviewer's job is to adjudicate the new match the same way these 31 were, not to add it.
_ownership.review_trigger: If the population grows past ~40 without a recorded adjudication per entry, the 'adjudicated' claim has stopped being true and this disposition should be revisited.
